reef.name: Lingcod & rockfish
reef.life_stage: Adult lingcod and recreationally targeted rockfish; rockfish species occupy different niches.
reef.habitat: Verified rocky reef, relief and adjoining edges are search leads. NOAA identifies rocky reef as important to lingcod and many rockfish, but a broad hard-bottom class or a historical camera window does not prove an occupied fishing pile.
reef.method: Sounder first, then a controlled bottom drift with your double-drop rig. For lingcod, investigate ledges and edges; for rockfish, also inspect suspended marks above the reef. Reset when bottom contact or boat control deteriorates.
reef.timing: Season, species-specific closures and in-season notices govern take; nesting and seasonal movement do not create a predictable bite window.
reef.condition_response: Wind, crossing swell and drift speed change whether a rig can remain near bottom without snagging. The planned drift must be revised from the boat's observed track and line angle.
evidence_needed: Identified species, depth and fish marks on the day
Measured drift, rig weight and bottom-contact time
Comparable successful and empty drifts; survey method and effort
reef.search_for: Search mapped rock relief and rock–sediment boundaries; inspect both the bottom and schools suspended above it.
reef.presentation: Use a controlled bottom drift for lingcod, and adjust the rig to the depth of identified rockfish marks. Reset when line angle prevents effective contact.
reef.caution: Rockfish species have different niches and restrictions; a terrain grade is not a catch probability.
required_to_confirm: Current legal access and method
Manageable fishing and return conditions
Identified species, depth and fish marks on the day
Measured drift, rig weight and bottom-contact time
Comparable successful and empty drifts; survey method and effort
reef.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.
reef.regional_notes: Crescent City, Mendocino and Point Reyes survey leads remain habitat context until native depth, substrate, MPA and chart screens are complete.
reef.depth_guidance: Follow the current management-area depth rule and the boat's qualified gear depth. Source grid resolution does not establish safe or fishable bottom.

pacific-halibut.name: Pacific halibut
pacific-halibut.life_stage: Adult shelf-feeding fish; not California halibut or a local nursery observation.
pacific-halibut.habitat: Shelf soft or mixed-bottom lanes with prey are broad search leads. Pacific halibut are not interchangeable with California halibut, and a California-halibut sediment area cannot be reused as its fishing spot.
pacific-halibut.method: On a legal shelf lane, use sonar to confirm depth and bottom, then test a controlled near-bottom bait or jig drift. Record line angle and whether fish and prey are actually observed.
pacific-halibut.timing: IPHC describes seasonal feeding and deeper winter spawning, but no fixed North Coast waypoint or universal depth follows. California quota closures can supersede a published season date.
pacific-halibut.condition_response: Near-bottom presentation requires measured drift control; full transit, fog, swell direction and return conditions still govern a trip.
evidence_needed: Verified shelf substrate and legal depth
Dated species and prey observations at the fishing location
Effort, including empty drifts and changing gear control
pacific-halibut.search_for: Review surveyed shelf sediment or mixed bottom within the trip depth and current legal area; confirm it with the sounder.
pacific-halibut.presentation: Make a short near-bottom test drift with legal gear, adjust weight for measured line angle, and move only on observed habitat or prey evidence.
pacific-halibut.caution: Do not reuse California-halibut points. Confirm quota, season, one-line/two-hook restriction and MPA access for the exact date.
required_to_confirm: Current legal access, quota and method
Manageable fishing and return conditions
Verified shelf substrate and legal depth
Dated species and prey observations at the fishing location
Effort, including empty drifts and changing gear control
pacific-halibut.tactics_basis: General IPHC biology and reviewed CDFW rules, not a local catch model or qualified fishing location.

source_links.title: IPHC stock biology and seasonal shelf migration
CDFW Pacific halibut rules and quota tracking

pacific-halibut.regional_notes: The Northern California and south-of-Point-Arena allocation split requires local date and quota review before a target is shown as open.
pacific-halibut.depth_guidance: A 200-foot boat limit is an equipment/plan constraint, not a Pacific-halibut optimum. Deeper shelf water needs its own qualified bottom and gear plan.

halibut.name: California halibut
halibut.life_stage: Coastal fish targeted by recreational anglers; nursery and trawl samples are distinct evidence.
halibut.habitat: CDFW identifies estuary and open-coast soft-bottom habitat. Connected sand or mud and edges can bound a search, but bottom type alone cannot establish fish presence.
halibut.method: Search an area with a controlled drift and a presentation near the seabed. Use the sounder to check the edge and bait; move between comparable depth bands when an area produces no evidence.
halibut.timing: Movement and El Niño conditions can shift distribution. A static historic polygon is not a current abundance map.
halibut.condition_response: Enough movement to cover ground can aid searching, but excess drift prevents effective near-bottom presentation; do not infer bottom current from tide height.
evidence_needed: Actual bait and fish observations at depth
Catch per fishing hour, including zero-catch attempts
halibut.search_for: Start on mapped shallow sand or mud, especially where bait occurs near a bottom transition.
halibut.presentation: Keep bait or a lure near the bottom on a controlled drift; change depth or location when bait and bottom contact are absent.
halibut.caution: Bottom temperature and current are not measured by the surface layer; confirm the actual depth with sonar.
required_to_confirm: Current legal access and method
Manageable fishing and return conditions
Sand/gravel and edge confirmation
Actual bait and fish observations at depth
Catch per fishing hour, including zero-catch attempts
halibut.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.
halibut.regional_notes: Treat California and Pacific halibut as distinct targets with separate rules and evidence.
halibut.depth_guidance: CDFW's broad 0–300 ft species range is not a location-specific depth optimum or an override of the user's fishing limit.

salmon.name: Chinook salmon
salmon.life_stage: Ocean-feeding fish; species and stock identification affect legal access.
salmon.habitat: Mobile water-column forage, shelf conditions and migration matter more than a fixed seafloor pin. A coastal sector is only a search reference.
salmon.method: Check the current local season, then use lawful gear to search observed bait and fish marks at their actual depth. Separate trolling presentation depth from seabed depth.
salmon.timing: Run timing and ocean survival vary by stock and year; an old landing or solunar rating cannot establish a present school.
salmon.condition_response: Evaluate offshore exposure, fog and the complete return window. Water-column presentation depth must not be confused with seabed depth.
salmon.search_for: Use recent legal-season forage and identified fish observations to choose coastal feeding water.
salmon.presentation: Use lawful trolling gear at observed bait and fish depth, checking the entire transit and return forecast.
salmon.caution: No fixed reef or modeled surface temperature establishes an active salmon school.
required_to_confirm: Current legal access and method
Manageable fishing and return conditions
Fresh forage and species observations
Stock/season context and fishing method
Search effort and zero-catch hours
salmon.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.
salmon.regional_notes: Northern river-stock context informs ecology but is not a current local salmon opening or catch forecast.
salmon.depth_guidance: Set presentation depth from observed marks and lawful gear, not a static 200- or 300-foot bottom contour.

dungeness.name: Dungeness crab
dungeness.life_stage: Adult-sized crabs; juvenile nursery habitat cannot be treated as a harvest hotspot.
dungeness.habitat: CDFW identifies sand and sand-mud adult habitat. A 2019–2021 pilot of 14 Northern and Central California commercial vessels found most modeled pot-setting at 40–120 m, but that describes sampled fleet behavior, not abundance, a recreational optimum or Morro Bay performance.
dungeness.method: When the season and chosen gear are permitted, compare a small number of sediment locations with consistent bait, gear and soak effort. Record empty sets as well as catches. Check bottom type and retrieval conditions before setting.
dungeness.timing: Opening, health and entanglement restrictions change independently; month in the commercial study reflects fleet decisions and regulations as well as crab availability.
dungeness.condition_response: Deeper gear increases line, buoy, handling and retrieval demands. Choose a band only when the boat can set and retrieve safely in the full trip conditions.
evidence_needed: Catch per trap-hour or hoop set by depth
Bait, soak time, size, sex and empty sets
Direct evidence of local predation; a poor catch alone cannot identify sea otters as the cause
dungeness.search_for: Search mapped sand and mud in a legal area and season, comparing depth and soak effort systematically.
dungeness.presentation: Use lawful crab gear suited to the actual depth and retrieve safely; log soak duration, bait, depth and empty sets.
dungeness.caution: Neither sea-otter presence nor deeper water alone establishes productive crab grounds.
required_to_confirm: Current legal access and method
Manageable fishing and return conditions
Catch per trap-hour or hoop set by depth
Bait, soak time, size, sex and empty sets
Direct evidence of local predation; a poor catch alone cannot identify sea otters as the cause
dungeness.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.
dungeness.regional_notes: The pilot under-sampled Point Arena, used GPS loggers rather than AIS, and cannot identify exact recreational hotspots. The article page's acceptance date conflicts with its publication date, so its bibliographic chronology needs editorial verification.
dungeness.depth_guidance: CDFW quality sampling includes 90, 150–180 and 210–240 ft strata. This supports a controlled deeper comparison, not a claim that 250–300 ft is best. Keep the current 200-ft fishing-plan ceiling unless a separate deeper crab plan passes gear, legal, source and safety gates.

albacore.name: Albacore tuna
albacore.life_stage: Surface-oriented fish encountered by West Coast troll fisheries; size and behavior vary.
albacore.habitat: Open-water temperature and oceanic fronts can narrow an offshore search. NOAA says juveniles often use fronts; a temperature contour alone is not a fish observation.
albacore.method: Compare recent SST, chlorophyll and current context, then look for actual bait, birds or fish. Start a search sector only after a fuel, range and return-weather plan; a colored front is not a catch location.
albacore.timing: Migration and fronts move; stale imagery and historical catches do not justify a persistent hotspot.
albacore.condition_response: Offshore distance, fuel reserve, visibility, swell and return weather matter more than a nearshore reef score. Missing imagery or model disagreement lowers confidence.
evidence_needed: Dated, cloud-screened fronts with native pixel size
Independent bait/fish sightings and catch effort
Fuel and range plan for the observed sea state
albacore.search_for: Prioritize ocean fronts and water transitions as search context for surface-oriented juveniles; look for forage and identified fish.
albacore.presentation: Use a searching troll or present bait at confirmed activity; compare both sides of a water transition rather than committing to a temperature number.
albacore.caution: Adult deep-water habitat and juvenile surface fisheries are different; fronts alone cannot confirm albacore.
required_to_confirm: Current legal access and method
Manageable fishing and return conditions
Dated, cloud-screened fronts with native pixel size
Independent bait/fish sightings and catch effort
Fuel and range plan for the observed sea state
albacore.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.
albacore.thermal_note: Broad juvenile eastern-Pacific tagged-fish envelope from the reviewed HMS synthesis, not an optimum.

source_links.title: NOAA HMS essential fish habitat synthesis

albacore.regional_notes: A fixed northern tuna polygon cannot predict fish on a selected future date; forecast water-mass evidence must be valid for the planned time.
albacore.depth_guidance: Water-column search and lure depth are distinct from seabed depth. Do not apply the bottom-fishing 200-ft ceiling to open-water tuna habitat.
